uslaw-usc-t2-s288h:
Section 288h of Title 2 of the United States Code charges the Senate Legal Counsel with defending certain constitutional powers. It sits in Chapter 9D of Title 2, current through Public Law 119-134. The defence is to be vigorous whenever the powers are placed in issue.

First comes the privilege from arrest, and from being questioned elsewhere, for any speech or debate, under Article I. Next come the powers of the Senate to judge the elections and fitness of its own members. The Senate may also punish or expel a member. The section adds the power to keep parts of the Senate journal secret, and to set the rules of its own work. It covers the power of Congress to make all laws needful to carry out its powers under the Constitution. It ends with the validity of acts of Congress.
